sessionName: Week 4 - Scoping calls and pitch discipline
summary: George Berrington reviewed sales execution with Thomas Avery and Grace Lindqvist. Pitches are written within 48 hours with little scoping, and fee negotiations usually end in a discount. We agreed a standard 30-minute scoping call before every pitch, a qualification check and rules for fee negotiation.

discussion.keyPoints: Grace's notes showed the scoping call often did not happen because the deal team was too busy. Thomas said the pitch then guesses at the IC questions.
Brookvale discounted on 14 of its last 20 wins, by 15 percent on average. George pointed out this contradicts the week 1 decision not to match discounts.
Thomas admitted Brookvale pitches on nearly every RFP, including auctions where the fund is unlikely to win the asset.

recommendations.recommendation: Hold a 30-minute scoping call with the deal partner before every pitch, covering the thesis, IC date and competing bidders.
Decline pitches where the fund is one of more than six bidders in a first-round auction and Brookvale has no prior relationship.
Offer scope reductions rather than discounts, with any discount above 5 percent approved by Thomas.
Use a two-page proposal with three scope options instead of the current 12-page document.
Have every director shadow two partner-led pitches a quarter.

actions.action: Draft the two-page, three-option proposal template
Write the discount approval rule into the engagement process

nextFocus: Restructure the pipeline to track pitch stages and conversion properly.
nextPreparation: Grace to export all pitches from the last 12 months with dates and outcomes.

tests.question: Is the rule on declining crowded auctions agreed?
What does the new proposal look like?
